s: In which State is the Palamau Tiger Reserve located?
x: Palamau is in Jharkhand; Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh and Askot in Uttarakhand.

s: Which of the following environmental issues is associated with the Satpura–Melghat tiger corridor?
o: Translocation of gaur from Central India
Expansion of mangrove vegetation into the corridor
Eviction of tribal communities by a biosphere-reserve order
Construction of railway lines through the corridor
x: Railway lines have been identified as cutting through the Satpura–Melghat tiger corridor.

s: Which State has the highest number of tiger reserves in India?
x: Madhya Pradesh has 9 tiger reserves, the highest number among Indian States.

s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body under which Act?
x: The NTCA is a statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, headed by the Environment Minister.

s: Which became India's 58th Tiger Reserve in 2025?
x: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla was the 56th, Ratapani the 57th (2024) and Madhav the 58th (2025).

s: Betla National Park forms the core of which tiger reserve?
x: Palamau in Jharkhand, one of the original nine Project Tiger reserves, has Betla National Park as its core.

s: As of 2026, how many Tiger Reserves did India have?
x: India had 58 Tiger Reserves (up from 9 in 1973), covering about 2.6% of its land.

s: India's wild tiger population in 2022 and its approximate share of the world's wild tigers were
x: The tiger count rose from 1,411 in 2006 to 3,682 in 2022, over 70% of the world's wild tigers. 1,411 is the 2006 figure; the other combinations are distractors.

s:
Consider the following statements about tiger reserves:
1. Melghat Tiger Reserve is in Maharashtra.
2. Pench Tiger Reserve spans Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.
3. Bandipur Tiger Reserve is in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Pench Tiger Reserve spans Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, not Telangana.

s:
Consider the following statements about tiger reserves:
1. Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam Tiger Reserve lies in both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
2. Amrabad Tiger Reserve is located in Telangana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 2 is correct. After bifurcation the Telangana part became Amrabad Tiger Reserve, so Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam now lies in Andhra Pradesh alone.

s: In which State is the Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve located?
x: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla is in Chhattisgarh; Manas and Orang are in Assam.

s: Which became India's 57th Tiger Reserve in 2024?
x: The order is Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla (56th), Ratapani (57th, 2024) and Madhav (58th, 2025).

s: Which is India's largest Tiger Reserve?
x: Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam is India's largest tiger reserve and lies in Andhra Pradesh alone after bifurcation.

s: In which year was Project Tiger launched with 9 tiger reserves?
x: Project Tiger began in 1973 with 9 reserves (18,278 sq km); India now has 58.

s: Which State has the largest number of tiger reserves?
x: Madhya Pradesh has the most tiger reserves (9).

s: Why is the possibility of human–tiger conflict in India growing?
o: All tigers now live within notified Tiger Reserves
Reserve boundaries have expanded to cover all tiger habitat
A growing share of tigers now live outside notified reserves
Tigers outside reserves are no longer part of conservation landscapes
x: A growing share of India's tigers lives outside notified reserves, raising the possibility of conflict with people.

s: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 with how many reserves?
x: Project Tiger began in 1973 with 9 reserves.

s: In which year was the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), a statutory body, set up?
x: NTCA was set up in 2006 under the amended Wildlife (Protection) Act.

s: What was India's average tiger count according to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022?
x: AITE 2022 gave an average of 3,682 tigers; 1,411 was the 2006 baseline.

s: Which is India's first tiger reserve, where Project Tiger was formally launched in 1973?
x: Project Tiger was formally launched at Corbett, India's first tiger reserve (1973).

s: Madhav, India's 58th tiger reserve (March 2025), is in which State?
x: Madhav in Madhya Pradesh became the 58th tiger reserve in March 2025.

s: Amangarh Tiger Reserve, a buffer of Corbett, lies in which State?
x: Amangarh is in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, as a buffer of Corbett.

s: Which is India's largest tiger reserve?
x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (AP) is the largest; Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla is third after NSTR and Manas.

s: What is M-STrIPES, used in India's tiger reserves?
o: An app-based patrolling and monitoring tool
x: M-STrIPES is an app-based patrolling and monitoring tool used in tiger reserves.

s: In which State is the Buxa Tiger Reserve located?
x: Buxa Tiger Reserve is in Alipurduar district of West Bengal.

s: In which State is the Indravati Tiger Reserve located?
x: Indravati Tiger Reserve is in Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh.

s: Which tiger reserve of Chhattisgarh became India's 56th tiger reserve in November 2024?
x: Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla was notified as the 56th tiger reserve in November 2024; it is India's third largest.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Satkosia Tiger Reserve lies in the Mahanadi gorge of Odisha.
2. Periyar Tiger Reserve is in Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Satkosia is in the Mahanadi gorge of Odisha; Periyar Tiger Reserve is in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

s: Ratapani, declared India's 57th tiger reserve in December 2024, is in which State?
x: Ratapani in Madhya Pradesh became the 57th tiger reserve in December 2024.

s: Which is the only tiger reserve of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has only one tiger reserve, NSTR; Rayala is its elephant reserve.

s: In which State is Valmiki Tiger Reserve located?
x: Valmiki is in Bihar; Nagarhole is in Karnataka and Ranthambore in Rajasthan.

s: In which hills does Periyar Tiger Reserve lie?
x: Periyar is in the Western Ghats; Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam is in the Nallamala Hills and Similipal in the Eastern Ghats.

s: Tadoba Tiger Reserve is associated with which landscape?
x: Tadoba lies in the Deccan and central Indian forest landscape of Maharashtra.

s: In which district of Maharashtra is the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve?
x: Tadoba-Andhari, one of the oldest tiger reserves, is in Chandrapur district.

s: Rajaji in Uttarakhand became India's tiger reserve of which number in 2015?
x: Rajaji became the 48th tiger reserve in 2015; Orang became the 49th.

s: Which were India's first Ramsar sites, designated in 1981?
x: Chilika and Keoladeo were India's first Ramsar sites (1981); Sukhna and Sauj Jheel are the latest (2026).

s: How many Ramsar sites did India have in October 2026?
x: India has 103 Ramsar sites after Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP) were added on 15 October 2026.

s: Where is Sukhna Wetland, one of India's latest Ramsar sites (October 2026)?
x: Sukhna Wetland is in Chandigarh; Sauj Jheel, added the same day, is in Uttar Pradesh.

s: As of August 2026, which Ramsar site became India’s 101st Ramsar site and Arunachal Pradesh’s first?
x: Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh became India’s 101st Ramsar site on 3 August 2026 and was the State’s first Ramsar site.

s: Which of the following is the Ramsar site of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh’s Ramsar site. Gogabeel is in Bihar, Glaw Lake is in Arunachal Pradesh, and Menar is in Rajasthan.

s: Kopra Reservoir is notable as which of the following?
o: The first Ramsar site of Andhra Pradesh
The first Ramsar site of Odisha
The first Ramsar site of Chhattisgarh
x: Kopra Reservoir is Chhattisgarh's first Ramsar site. AP's only Ramsar site is Kolleru (2002), India's first was Chilika (1981), and Kopra has no link to Odisha.

s: Which Ramsar site is correctly matched with its State?
x: Kopra Reservoir is in Chhattisgarh. Surha Tal and Shekha Jheel are in Uttar Pradesh; Khichan and Menar are in Rajasthan.

s: How many listed Ramsar sites does Odisha have?
x: Odisha has six: Chilika, Bhitarkanika, Ansupa, Tampara, Hirakud and Satkosia Gorge.

s: Which wetland became India's 100th Ramsar site on 5 June 2026?
x: Surha Tal (JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary), Ballia, UP, was the 100th; Shekha Jheel was 99th and Glaw Lake 101st.

s: Shekha Jheel, India's 99th Ramsar site (April 2026), is in which State?
x: Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh became the 99th Ramsar site in April 2026.

s: Sasthamkotta Ramsar site is in which State?
x: Sasthamkotta is in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

s: Which Ramsar site is wrongly matched with its State?
x: Menar, added in 2025, is in Rajasthan; the other pairs are correct.

s: Glaw Lake, Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, lies inside which tiger reserve?
x: Glaw Lake, India's 101st Ramsar site (Aug 2026), lies inside Kamlang Tiger Reserve and is home to the white-bellied heron.

s: In which year were 28 new Indian wetlands declared Ramsar sites in a single year?
x: In 2022, 28 new Indian wetlands got Ramsar status, the largest addition in one year.

s: How many Ramsar sites did India have as of August 2026?
x: Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh became the 101st Indian Ramsar site on 3 August 2026.

s: In which State/UT is the Hokera wetland, a Ramsar site, located?
x: Hokera, in the Jhelum basin, is in Jammu and Kashmir, not Punjab.

s:
Match the following Ramsar sites with their States:
List-I (Ramsar site)
A. Rudrasagar
B. Renuka
C. Thol Lake
D. Karaivetti
List-II (State)
1. Gujarat
2. Tamil Nadu
3. Tripura
4. Himachal Pradesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Rudrasagar is in Tripura, Renuka in Himachal Pradesh, Thol Lake in Gujarat and Karaivetti in Tamil Nadu.

s: Which is the largest inland saline wetland of India, a Ramsar site in Rajasthan?
x: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland saline wetland and a flamingo wintering site.

s: Khichan, a Ramsar site in Rajasthan, is known for which wintering birds?
x: Thousands of demoiselle cranes winter at Khichan in Rajasthan.

s: Gogabeel, an ox-bow lake that is both a Ramsar site and a Community Reserve, is in which State?
x: Gogabeel is an ox-bow lake in Bihar, a Ramsar site and also a Community Reserve.

s: In which State is the Patna Bird Sanctuary (Etah), a Ramsar site, located?
x: Patna Bird Sanctuary is in Etah district of Uttar Pradesh, not in Bihar.

s: Which was India's first Ramsar site, designated in 1981?
x: Chilika became India's first Ramsar site in 1981; Corbett was the first Tiger Reserve (1973) and Glaw Lake the newest Ramsar site (2026).

s: In which country is Ramsar, where the Convention on wetlands was signed on 2 February 1971?
x: The Ramsar Convention was signed on 2 February 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

s: In which year was the Ramsar Convention on wetlands adopted at Ramsar, Iran?
x: The Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; India joined in 1982.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ramsar definition of a wetland?
o: It includes marshes, fens and peatlands
It includes fresh, brackish or salt water
It includes marine water up to 6 metres deep at low tide
It covers only natural water bodies, not artificial ones
x: The Ramsar definition covers both natural and artificial water bodies.

s: Under the judicial restriction described for Ramsar sites, mining within 10 km requires approval from which authority or authorities?
o: Only the State Pollution Control Board
District Collector and Gram Sabha alone
x: Mining within 10 km requires approval from the National Board for Wildlife and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

s: On which day is World Wetlands Day, marking the adoption of the Ramsar Convention, observed every year?
x: World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February. 22 March is World Water Day, 5 June is World Environment Day and 22 April is Earth Day.

s: The Ramsar Convention of 1971 is concerned with the conservation and wise use of what?
x: The Ramsar Convention, adopted at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971, is for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

s: In which year did India become a party to the Ramsar Convention?
x: India joined in 1982; the Convention was adopted in 1971 and Chilika was designated in 1981.

s: Under the Ramsar definition, a wetland includes marine water up to what depth at low tide?
x: Ramsar wetlands include marine water up to 6 m deep at low tide, and may be natural or artificial.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ramsar Convention?
o: It was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran
World Wetlands Day is observed on 22 March
Artificial water bodies can qualify as wetlands
Keoladeo and Loktak are India's Montreux Record sites
x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February; 22 March is World Water Day.

s: Which two Indian wetlands are on the Montreux Record?
x: India's Montreux Record entries are Keoladeo (Rajasthan) and Loktak (Manipur).

s: What is the Montreux Record?
o: A register of Ramsar sites where changes in ecological character have occurred or are likely
A list of wetlands that are also World Heritage Sites
A list of newly designated Ramsar sites of each year
A register of wetlands shared by two or more countries
x: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites whose ecological character is changing because of pollution, technology or other human interference.

s: Where does the black-necked crane breed?
x: The black-necked crane breeds in Ladakh; the Siberian crane wintered at Keoladeo.

s: Which national park was the wintering ground of the Siberian Crane in India?
x: The Siberian Crane used to winter at Keoladeo National Park, Bharatpur, Rajasthan.

s: Which bird was declared the State bird of Ladakh in 2021?
x: The black-necked crane breeds in Ladakh and became the UT's State bird in 2021.

s: Where did India, a key wintering ground on the Central Asian Flyway, host CMS COP13 in 2020?
x: India hosted the 13th Conference of the Convention on Migratory Species at Gandhinagar in 2020.

s: Which bird breeds on high Central Asian lakes and crosses the Himalaya to winter in India?
x: The Bar-headed goose, one of the highest-flying birds, crosses the Himalaya to winter in India. The Amur falcon winters in southern Africa.

s: Where does the Amur falcon, which makes the longest raptor migration, spend the winter?
x: It migrates from south-east Siberia and northern China to southern Africa, stopping over in Nagaland in October–November.

s: In which State does the Amur falcon make a stopover during October-November on its migration?
x: Amur falcons stop over in Nagaland (Doyang, Pangti) on their way to winter in southern Africa.

s: Which organisation designates Important Bird Areas globally, and which organisation is its Indian partner?
x: Important Bird Areas are a BirdLife International designation, with the Bombay Natural History Society as its Indian partner.

s: Telineelapuram and Telukunchi in Andhra Pradesh are Important Bird Areas principally associated with breeding populations of which birds?
x: Telineelapuram and Telukunchi in Srikakulam are Important Bird Areas for breeding painted storks and spot-billed pelicans.

s: The mass mortality of migratory birds at Sambhar Lake in November 2019 was caused by which disease?
x: The mass death of migratory birds at Sambhar Lake was attributed to avian botulism.

s: The Rushikulya mouth Important Bird Area in Odisha is particularly known for which phenomenon?
x: The Rushikulya mouth hosts the olive ridley arribada, the mass nesting congregation of olive ridley turtles.

s: Which of the following bird sanctuaries is NOT in Kerala?
x: Ranganathittu is in Karnataka; Kumarakom, Thattekad and Mangalavanam are in Kerala.

s: Which of the following bird sanctuaries does NOT lie, even partly, in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Vedanthangal is in Tamil Nadu; Nelapattu, Kolleru and Pulicat (on the border) include Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which bird sanctuary is regarded as India's oldest water-bird sanctuary, established in 1858?
x: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu is regarded as India's oldest water-bird sanctuary, established in 1858.

s: In which State is the Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary located?
x: Nelapattu is in Andhra Pradesh; Vedanthangal is in Tamil Nadu, Ranganathittu in Karnataka and Sultanpur in Haryana.

s: On the border of which two States does the Pulicat Bird Sanctuary lie?
x: Pulicat is on the AP–Tamil Nadu border; Kolleru is in AP, Bharatpur in Rajasthan and Nalsarovar in Gujarat.

s: Bharatpur (Keoladeo) Bird Sanctuary is located in which State?
x: Bharatpur (Keoladeo) is in Rajasthan, not Haryana; Sultanpur is the Haryana sanctuary.

s: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is located in which State?
x: Ranganathittu is on Kaveri islets in Mandya, Karnataka.

s: In which State is the Nal Sarovar Bird Sanctuary located?
x: Nal Sarovar Bird Sanctuary is in Gujarat.

s: Pitti, a seabird islet sanctuary, is in which Union Territory?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
x: Pitti is a small seabird islet sanctuary in Lakshadweep.

s: Udhwa Bird Sanctuary is located in which State?
x: Udhwa Bird Sanctuary is in Sahibganj district of Jharkhand.

s: Which bird sanctuary of India is a Ramsar site (1981) and also a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Keoladeo (Bharatpur) in Rajasthan became a Ramsar site in 1981 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

s: Gir, the only natural home of the Asiatic lion, is in which State?
x: Gir is in Gujarat. Bhitarkanika and Gahirmatha are the Odisha sites.

s: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh is known chiefly for which species?
o: Olive ridley turtle and saltwater crocodile
x: Rollapadu protects the Great Indian Bustard and blackbuck. Gharial and dolphin belong to National Chambal, the Asiatic lion to Gir, and olive ridleys and saltwater crocodiles to the Odisha coast (Gahirmatha, Bhitarkanika).

s: In which year was Project Lion, for the Asiatic lion of Gir, launched?
x: Project Lion was launched in 2020; Gir in Gujarat is the only natural home of the Asiatic lion.

s: For which of the following is Bhitarkanika in Odisha chiefly known?
x: Bhitarkanika is known for saltwater crocodiles and mangroves; olive ridley nesting is at Gahirmatha.

s: Which species does the National Chambal Sanctuary chiefly protect?
x: National Chambal (Rajasthan–MP–UP) protects the gharial and the Gangetic dolphin.

s: Gahirmatha on the Odisha coast is famous for the mass nesting of which species?
x: Gahirmatha is known for the arribada (mass nesting) of olive ridley turtles; Bhitarkanika is known for crocodiles.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about elephant reserves (ERs) in India?
o: Odisha's ERs are Mayurbhanj, Mahanadi and Sambalpur
Stored carbon in ERs has risen by about 38%
ERs are notified only in areas outside tiger reserves
x: Elephant reserves overlap tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests, so they are not limited to areas outside tiger reserves.

s: How many elephant reserves does India have, spread over 14 States?
x: There are 33 elephant reserves in 14 States under Project Elephant (1992).

s: Which two States have the most elephant reserves, five each?
x: Assam and Tamil Nadu have 5 elephant reserves each; Odisha has 3.

s: According to the DNA-based census of October 2025, which State has the largest wild elephant population?
x: The census counted 22,446 wild elephants, with Karnataka having the largest population.

s: According to the DNA-based census of October 2025, about how many wild elephants does India have?
x: The DNA-based census (Oct 2025) counted 22,446 wild elephants in India.

s: Which is Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve, which includes Koundinya WLS?
x: AP's one elephant reserve is Rayala (incl. Koundinya WLS); its biosphere reserve is Seshachalam and its tiger reserve NSTR.

s: Which is the only biosphere reserve of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Seshachalam (2010) is Andhra Pradesh's only biosphere reserve; Rayala is its elephant reserve.

s: In which year was Project Elephant launched?
x: Project Elephant began in February 1992; it has 33 elephant reserves in 14 States.

s: Residual (in situ) soils dominate which part of India?
x: Residual soils dominate Peninsular India, while drifted (ex situ) soils dominate North India.

s: How many major soil types are recognised in India's classification?
x: Eight: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.

s: Which of the following crops is NOT typically grown on alluvial soil?
x: Coffee is grown on the red and laterite soils of the Western Ghats; wheat, rice and sugarcane suit alluvial soil.

s: Which is the most widespread soil of India?
x: Alluvial soil covers about 45.6% of India, the largest share of any soil type.

s: Alluvial soil, the most widespread soil of India, covers about what share of the country's area?
x: Alluvial soil covers about 15 lakh sq km, about 45.6% of India's area.

s: Black (regur) soil covers about what share of India's area?
x: Black soil covers about 5.47 lakh sq km, about 16.6% of India.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the alluvial belts of the northern plains?
o: Khadar is new alluvium deposited by floods
Bhabar is a marshy lowland lying south of the Tarai
Bhangar is old alluvium on higher ground beyond normal flood reach
Streams sink and disappear in the pebbly Bhabar belt
x: Bhabar is the pebbly foothill belt where streams sink; the marshy Tarai lies south of it, not the other way round.

s:
Assertion (A): Khadar is generally more fertile than Bhangar.
Reason (R): Khadar is renewed frequently through flood deposition.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: fresh flood silt renews Khadar every year, keeping it more fertile than old Bhangar.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Khadar – Marshy lowland south of Bhabar
Bhangar – New alluvium deposited by floods
Bhabar – Coarse alluvial belt where streams disappear
Tarai – Old alluvium with calcareous concretions
x: Bhabar is the coarse belt where streams disappear. Khadar is new flood alluvium, Bhangar old alluvium with kankar and Tarai the marshy land south of Bhabar.

s: What type of deposits are the Karewa soils of the Kashmir Valley?
x: Karewas are lacustrine deposits of gravel and mud on plateaus above the Jhelum plains.

s: Kankar (calcareous concretions) is a feature of which of the following?
x: Kankar belongs to Bhangar, the old alluvium; the claim that Khadar holds calcareous deposits is false.

s: Karewa soils of the Kashmir Valley are famous for the cultivation of which crop?
x: Karewa soils (old lake-bed deposits) are famous for saffron at Pampore, besides almonds and walnuts.

s: Which of the following groups contains only micronutrients tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
o: Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur and zinc
Calcium, magnesium, sodium, nitrogen and phosphorus
Carbon, oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen and potassium
Zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron
x: The micronutrients listed are zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron. Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur are separately included among the tested nutrients.

s: Most Indian soils are deficient in which combination of constituents, thereby contributing to the emphasis on Soil Health Cards?
x: Most Indian soils lack nitrogen, phosphorus and humus. This deficiency is one of the reasons for promoting Soil Health Cards.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about conservation agriculture?
o: It may involve minimum or zero tillage
Crop residue is retained as soil cover
It requires complete removal of crop residues
x: Conservation agriculture retains crop residues; removing them completely is contrary to the practice.

s: What does strip cropping involve?
o: Planting only trees in long strips across a watershed
Constructing permanent dams across every field channel
Alternating erosion-resistant crop strips, such as grass, with row-crop strips
x: Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-resistant crops, such as grass, with row crops to reduce wind- and water-induced erosion.

s: Which one of the following is a benefit of crop rotation?
o: It improves soil fertility, reduces pests and helps prevent soil erosion
It removes the need for any soil cover
It is used only to reclaim alkaline soils
x: Crop rotation improves fertility, cuts pest build-up and helps prevent erosion. It does not raise salinity, does not replace soil cover, and alkaline soils are reclaimed with gypsum, not by rotation alone.

s: Which soil-conservation measure traps sediment and checks gully growth?
x: Check dams trap sediment and check gully growth; shelter belts are tree rows that cut wind speed.

s: Which remedy is matched with deforestation?
x: Deforestation pairs with afforestation; soil erosion with soil stabilisation, habitat destruction with restoration and biodiversity loss with conservation.

s: For what purpose are China's straw checkerboards used?
x: Straw checkerboards are used to stabilise dunes and control movement of desert sands.

s: For which type of land is contour ploughing (contour bunding) used as a soil conservation method?
o: Low flat plains close to rivers
x: Contour ploughing and bunding along contour lines slow runoff on hilly, sloping, rainfed land.

s: Which soil conservation method uses rows of trees to cut wind speed in arid western India?
x: Shelter belts are rows of trees that break the force of wind and check wind erosion.

s: What does soil conservation mean?
o: Protecting soil from harm by controlling erosion and keeping its fertility high
Removing all crop residues from the field
Adding only chemical fertilisers to the soil
x: Soil conservation means both controlling erosion and keeping soil fertility high.

s: Which one of the following current agricultural practices is being promoted in Kurnool to conserve soil moisture?
o: Permanent flood irrigation with gypsum application
x: Kurnool is promoting Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing on a target area of 92,000 acres along with Jeevamrutham to conserve soil moisture.

s: How many parameters are tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
x: The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.

s: In which year did the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) begin?
x: IWMP started in 2009-10 and was merged into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY in 2015-16.

s: Where was the Soil Health Card scheme launched on 19 February 2015?
x: It was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan; cards are issued every two years and the slogan is 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa'.

s: How often are Soil Health Cards issued to farmers?
x: Soil Health Cards are issued every two years and test 12 parameters.

s: Which State had issued the most Soil Health Cards as of February 2026?
x: Of 25.79 crore cards generated by February 2026, Uttar Pradesh issued the most.

s: What is the slogan of the Soil Health Card scheme?
x: The Soil Health Card scheme, launched at Suratgarh in 2015, has the slogan 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa'.

s: Into which scheme was the Integrated Watershed Management Programme merged in 2015-16?
x: IWMP (2009-10) became the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY in 2015-16.

s: About how many Soil Health Cards had been generated in India as of February 2026?
x: 25.79 crore Soil Health Cards were generated by February 2026.

s: Regur soil, formed from the weathering of Deccan Trap basalt, is best suited to which group of crops?
x: Regur (black cotton) soil from Deccan basalt is suited to cotton, jowar, chillies and tobacco. Tea, coffee and rubber suit manured laterite; ragi and groundnut are typical of red soil; rice and jute are typical of alluvial soil.

s: From the weathering of which rock is black (regur) soil mainly formed?
x: Black soil comes from weathered Deccan Trap basalt and is neutral to alkaline.

s: Which of the following region–soil pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Thar Desert of western Rajasthan – Arid soil
Himalayan and hilly regions – Mountain or forest soil
Coastal and deltaic plains – Alluvial soil
x: The Deccan lava plateau has black soil, not alluvial soil.

s: Which soil is known for deep summer cracks and its 'self-ploughing' character?
x: Black soil has over 62% clay, high moisture retention, deep summer cracks and a self-ploughing character.

s: In which part of India are very deep black soils found?
x: Very deep black soils lie in the north-western Deccan Plateau.

s: Black (regur) soil contains clay of more than how much?
x: Black soil has more than 62% clay, giving it the highest moisture retention.

s: In which group of States are black soils mainly found?
x: Black (regur) soil covers the Deccan Plateau: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, western AP and north Karnataka.

s: Which one of the following sets contains nutrients in which black soil is comparatively rich?
x: Black soil is comparatively rich in calcium, potassium and magnesium, but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.

s: Which Indian soil has the highest moisture retention?
x: Black soil, with over 62% clay, has the highest moisture retention.

s: Which State has the largest tracts of black cotton soil formed on the Deccan Trap?
x: The Deccan Trap basalt of Maharashtra has given rise to the largest black cotton soil tracts.

s: What gives red soils their red colour?
x: Iron oxide makes these soils red; they look yellow when hydrated. They form from granite and gneiss.

s: Laterite soil is formed under which combination of conditions?
o: Waterlogging and accumulation of organic matter in humid lowlands
Low rainfall and low temperature with deposition of salts
Heavy leaching, rainfall above 200 cm and high temperature
x: Laterite forms through intense leaching under heavy rainfall exceeding 200 cm and high temperature.

s: Which one of the following statements about laterite soil is correct?
o: It is generally fertile without manuring and is rich in nitrogen and phosphate
It is rich in iron and aluminium oxides and is generally acidic and infertile
It is formed mainly from river deposits and contains abundant kankar
It has the highest moisture retention among Indian soils
x: Laterite soil is rich in iron and aluminium oxides but is generally acidic and infertile. It is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium and has excess iron oxide and potash.

s: Where does laterite soil mainly occur in India?
o: Summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats
x: Laterite soil occurs on the summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats; the Northern Plains have alluvial, the Deccan lava plateau black and the crystalline Peninsula red soil.

s: When adequately manured, laterite soil supports which group of crops?
x: Laterite soil can support tea, coffee, rubber and cashew when adequately manured.

s: When does red and yellow soil look yellow?
x: The red colour comes from iron oxide; it turns yellow when hydrated.

s: From which rocks are the red and yellow soils of India mainly formed?
x: Red and yellow soils form on crystalline granite and gneiss under low rainfall.

s:
Consider the following statements about red and yellow soils:
1. They develop on granite and gneiss under low rainfall.
2. They have high moisture retention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Red soils form on granite and gneiss; they are porous with low moisture retention, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Which group of crops is mainly grown on red and yellow soils?
x: Red and yellow soils mainly support ragi, groundnut and tobacco.

s: Why is laterite used as a building material?
o: Has high moisture retention and expands in water
Is composed entirely of river-borne sand
Can be cut into bricks that harden on exposure to air
Contains abundant organic matter and remains soft when dry
x: Laterite can be cut into bricks, which harden when exposed to air, making it useful as a building material.

s: In which nutrient is the laterite soil of Andhra Pradesh notably poor?
x: Laterite is poor in nitrogen but has excess iron oxide and potash; 'N is plentiful in AP laterite' is wrong.

s: Why is tea grown on hill slopes?
o: It needs slightly acidic soil and cannot bear standing water
It needs alkaline soil rich in calcium
It grows best in saline soil
x: Tea needs slightly acidic soil without calcium and good drainage, so it is grown on hill slopes.

s: On which soils is coffee mainly grown in the Western Ghats?
x: Coffee grows on the red and laterite soils of the Western Ghats, not on alluvial soil.

s: Red soils cover about what share of Andhra Pradesh's cultivated area?
x: Red soils cover about 60%; black soils about 25%, deltaic alluvium 5–6% and laterite about 1%.

s: How many agro-climatic zones does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has six agro-climatic zones.

s: Reh, kallar and usar are local names for which soils?
x: Reh, kallar and usar are saline/alkaline soils formed by over-irrigation and poor drainage.

s: What is the major cause of salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging in irrigated areas?
o: Scientific irrigation combined with adequate drainage
Excessive crop rotation and contour farming
x: Unscientific irrigation practices combined with inadequate drainage promote salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging.

s: Which one of the following groups contains the states identified as affected by salinity and alkalinity problems?
o: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Assam and Sikkim
Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Nagaland and Manipur
x: The affected states listed are Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Canal-irrigated Punjab experienced salinity and alkalinity after the Green Revolution.

s: In the FAO's Status of the World's Soil Resources 2026 report, soil-biodiversity loss ranks at which position among seven threats to soil?
o: Fourth, after erosion, SOC loss and nutrient mismanagement
x: The FAO 2026 report ranks soil-biodiversity loss 4th of 7 threats, after erosion, soil organic carbon loss and nutrient mismanagement. It is not first, second or last.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Alkaline soil — lime as the principal amendment
Acidic soil — salt-tolerant crops as the sole reclamation measure
x: Gypsum is used to reclaim alkaline or sodic soils, while lime is used for acidic soils. Drainage, leaching and salt-tolerant crops can also assist reclamation.

s: Which cause of land degradation is correctly matched with the States it affects?
x: Overgrazing affects Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra; over-irrigation Punjab, Haryana and western UP; mining Jharkhand, Odisha, MP and Chhattisgarh.

s: Which organisation prepared the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of June 2021?
x: The atlas was prepared by ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad.

s: As per the 2021 Desertification Atlas, what share of India's land was degraded in 2018-19?
x: About 97.85 mha (29.7%) was degraded in 2018-19, up from 28.76% in 2003-05.

s: According to the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas (2021), which is the largest driver of land degradation in India?
x: The SAC atlas names water erosion as the largest driver of land degradation in India.

s: As per the Desertification Atlas of June 2021, in how many of the 31 States/UTs did desertification rise?
x: Desertification rose in 28 of 31 States/UTs, according to the 2021 atlas.

s: Wind erosion is generally most severe under which combination of conditions?
o: Mulched soil, low wind speed and frequent light rain
Waterlogged soil, gentle winds and heavy forest cover
Bare, dry, fine-textured soil with strong and frequent winds
Dense vegetation, moist clayey soil and weak winds
x: Wind erosion is worst where soil is bare, dry and fine-textured and winds are strong and frequent.

s: Which rainfall factor generally matters more for the rate of soil erosion?
x: Rainfall intensity generally matters more than total annual rainfall for soil erosion.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes sheet erosion?
o: Subsurface removal of soil resulting in sinkholes
Formation of deep trenches by concentrated surface flow
Downslope movement of soil under gravity
Removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil by overland flow
x: Sheet erosion removes a thin top layer uniformly through overland flow. It is widespread and generally the least noticeable form of erosion.

s: Which is the final, most advanced stage of water erosion?
x: Water erosion progresses from splash to sheet, then rill and finally gully erosion.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Parts of Australia and Africa — sheet erosion
x: Parts of Australia and Africa are associated with tunnel erosion, in which subsurface removal may create sinkholes, not sheet erosion.

s: What is the RUSLE model used to predict?
x: RUSLE predicts long-term water erosion on slopes; ICAR has prepared national C- and P-factor maps for it.

s: Why can very intense bursts of rainfall make soil drier?
o: Always infiltrate completely and recharge the soil
Exceed infiltration capacity, causing runoff or evaporation instead of recharge
Convert all soil organic carbon directly into clay
Prevent surface water from moving downslope
x: When rainfall intensity exceeds infiltration capacity, water runs off or evaporates rather than recharging the soil. This drying effect can offset the benefit of greater annual rainfall.

s: Which type of soil erosion is widespread but the least noticed?
x: Sheet erosion removes a thin uniform topsoil layer and is the least noticed; gully erosion is the final stage.

s: Which is the most powerful agent of soil erosion?
x: Water is the most powerful erosion agent.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rainfall intensity matters more than total rainfall for soil erosion.
2. Sheet erosion is the final stage of water erosion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rainfall intensity matters more than total rainfall; gully erosion, not sheet erosion, is the final stage.

s: Arid (desert) soil is sandy and deficient in which of the following?
x: Arid soil is sandy and poor in nitrogen and humus, improves with irrigation, and has kankar at lower depths.

s: Which one of the following best describes forest and mountain soils?
o: Deep black soils formed from basalt in the Deccan Trap
Sandy soils rich in nitrogen and humus in western Rajasthan
Humus-rich soils on slopes, generally poor in potash and phosphorus
Salt-crusted soils of the coastal deltas
x: Forest and mountain soils are humus-rich, occur on slopes and are generally poor in potash and phosphorus. Mountain meadow soils may occur above the tree line.

s: What are peaty and marshy soils, found in Alappuzha-Kottayam and the Sundarbans, typically like?
x: Peaty soils form under heavy rain and waterlogging; they are black, heavy and highly acidic, not alkaline.

s: Which group consists only of soils generally described as acidic?
x: Laterite, peaty and forest soils are generally acidic. Black soil and saline-alkaline soils are neutral to alkaline, and arid, alluvial and red soils are not listed as acidic, so every other group includes a non-acidic soil.

s: Which soil of India has kankar at lower depths and is rich in phosphorus but poor in nitrogen and humus?
x: Desert soil is sandy, rich in phosphorus, poor in nitrogen and humus, with kankar at lower depths.

s: Which Indian soil is rich in phosphorus?
x: Desert soil, though poor in nitrogen and humus, is rich in phosphorus; black, red and laterite soils are poor in it.

s: Under which conditions do peaty soils develop?
o: Heavy rainfall, high humidity and good vegetation
Low rainfall and strong wind action
Heavy leaching on high hill summits
x: Peaty soils form where heavy rain, high humidity and good vegetation let organic matter build up faster than it rots.

s: Which soil order covers the largest share of India's area?
x: Inceptisols cover 39.7%, ahead of Entisols (28.1%), Alfisols (13.6%) and Vertisols (8.5%).

s: Which is the smallest soil order in India?
x: Mollisols are India's smallest soil order; Inceptisols are the largest.

s: In the ICAR/USDA classification, Vertisols correspond to which Indian soil?
x: Vertisols are the black soils, covering about 8.5% of India.

s: Arrange the soil horizons from the surface downward in the correct order.
x: The normal sequence is O, A, B, C and R: organic litter, topsoil, subsoil, weathered parent material and bedrock.

s: Which horizon of a soil profile is primarily characterised by the accumulation of minerals washed down from upper layers?
x: The B horizon is the subsoil zone where minerals washed down from upper horizons accumulate.

s: Which one of the following represents the approximate volume composition of a good soil?
o: Mineral matter 45%, organic matter 5%, water 25%, air 25%
Mineral matter 50%, organic matter 25%, water 15%, air 10%
Mineral matter 25%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 5%
Mineral matter 5%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 25%
x: A good soil is approximately composed of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air by volume.

s: Which of the following is a role of soil organic carbon?
x: Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, raises infiltration and feeds microbes.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five factors of soil formation?
x: The five factors are parent material, climate, relief, organisms and time; soil colour is a property, not a factor.

s: Limestone giving rise to calcium-rich soil shows the influence of which soil-formation factor?
x: Parent rock passes on its traits, e.g. limestone gives calcium-rich soil.

s: India's average soil organic carbon reportedly fell over 70 years from 1% to what level?
x: India's average SOC reportedly fell from 1% to 0.3% over 70 years.

s: What is the downward movement of water through the soil called?
x: Infiltration is entry of water at the surface; percolation is its movement down through the soil.

s: In which State are the Panna diamond mines located?
x: India's diamond mines are at Panna and Satna in Madhya Pradesh.

s: For which mineral is Panna in Madhya Pradesh known?
x: Panna is known for diamonds; Koderma for mica, Keonjhar for manganese and Sukinda for chromite.

s: With which mineral are the Zawar mines associated?
x: Zawar is associated with lead-zinc; Koderma with mica, Bailadila with iron ore and Khetri with copper.

s: For which minerals are the beach sands of Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam known?
o: Ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite
x: These beach sands contain ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite.

s: The world-class beach sand mineral deposits of Kerala lie between which two places?
x: Kerala's world-class beach sands (ilmenite, zircon, sillimanite) lie between Neendakara and Kayamkulam.

s: Where is the IREL unit that makes Kerala the largest thorium producer located?
x: IREL at Udyogamandal, Aluva processes monazite, making Kerala the largest thorium producer.

s: In which State is the Khetri copper area located?
x: Khetri (Jhunjhunu) is in Rajasthan; Malanjkhand is the copper area of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand's copper is in Singhbhum.

s: Bastar, Bilaspur, Dantewada and Jashpur are bauxite areas of which State?
x: All four are bauxite areas of Chhattisgarh.

s: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are bauxite areas of which State?
x: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are Odisha bauxite areas.

s: Which of the following is still worked as India's main gold mine?
x: Hutti in Karnataka is India's main working gold mine; the Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001.

s: For which mineral is Mainpat in Surguja district of Chhattisgarh known?
x: Surguja has bauxite at Mainpat; Dantewada in Chhattisgarh has tin.

s: Which is the only tin-producing State of India?
x: Chhattisgarh (Dantewada) is the only tin producer, though Haryana holds the larger share of resources.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rajasthan's minerals?
o: It is the sole producer of lead-zinc ores
Zawar near Udaipur is a lead-zinc area
It is the sole producer of copper ore
Khetri in Jhunjhunu is a copper area
x: Rajasthan is the sole lead-zinc producer, not the sole copper producer; MP ranks first in copper ore.

s: Lohardaga in Jharkhand is an important area of which mineral?
x: Lohardaga is Jharkhand's bauxite area; Jaduguda and Turamdih are uranium.

s: Which State is first in copper ore production, with the Malanjkhand mine?
x: Madhya Pradesh is first in copper ore (IMYB 2024) thanks to Malanjkhand in Balaghat; Rajasthan has the most copper resources.

s: Where was uranium first found in India, in 1951?
x: Uranium was first found at Jaduguda in Jharkhand in 1951.

s: Which State holds about 93% of India's nickel resources?
x: About 93% of India's nickel resources are in Odisha.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Mine)
A. Turamdih
B. Kudremukh
C. Malanjkhand
D. Lapsa Buru
List-II (Mineral)
1. Copper
2. Kyanite
3. Uranium
4. Iron ore
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Turamdih is uranium, Kudremukh iron ore, Malanjkhand copper and Lapsa Buru kyanite.

s: In which year was the Kolar gold mine closed?
x: The Kolar gold field closed in 2001; Hutti is now the main working gold mine.

s: In which form does thorium occur in Indian beach sands?
x: Thorium occurs as monazite and titanium as ilmenite in beach sands.

s: Which one of the following groups of minerals is characteristically associated with placer deposits?
x: Gold, tin and platinum are associated with placer deposits formed in alluvial sands. Coal, gypsum and salt are typical of sedimentary beds, while copper and lead commonly occur in veins or lodes.

s: How are bauxite deposits generally formed?
x: Residual weathering may produce laterite-linked bauxite; veins/lodes give tin, copper, zinc and lead.

s: Which of the following metals is NOT found in the free (native) state?
x: Aluminium is very reactive and found combined, mainly as bauxite; gold, silver and platinum occur native.

s: In which type of deposit do coal, gypsum, salt and potash usually occur?
x: Coal, gypsum, salt and potash occur in sedimentary beds; placers hold gold, tin and platinum.

s: Which of the following metals is too reactive ever to be found free in nature?
x: K, Na, Ca, Mg and Al are at the top of the reactivity series and never occur free; Au, Ag and Pt occur native.

s: What is the chemical formula of dolomite?
x: Dolomite is CaMg(CO₃)₂; magnesite is MgCO₃, rock salt NaCl and carnallite KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O.

s: Rock salt is an ore of which metal?
x: Sodium comes from rock salt; potassium from sylvine and carnallite, magnesium from magnesite and calcium from limestone.

s:
Arrange the following iron ores in descending order of their approximate iron content:
A. Siderite
B. Magnetite
C. Limonite
D. Haematite
x: Magnetite has up to about 70–72 per cent iron, haematite about 60–70 per cent, limonite 40–60 per cent and siderite is the lowest-grade ore.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding iron ores is correct?
o: Limonite is an iron carbonate and the lowest-grade ore.
Haematite is the most used commercially among the principal iron ores.
Siderite is a hydrated iron oxide containing 40–60 per cent iron.
Magnetite is non-magnetic and contains the least iron.
x: Haematite is the most commercially used iron ore. Limonite is hydrated, siderite is iron carbonate and magnetite is magnetic and high-grade.

s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

Ore — Metal
x: Rutile is a source of titanium, not thorium. Thorium and rare earths are associated with monazite.

s: Carnallite is an ore of which metals?
x: Carnallite (KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O) is an ore of both potassium and magnesium.

s: Which of the following ore–formula pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Malachite is the basic carbonate Cu₂(CO₃)(OH)₂; Cu₂S is chalcocite.

s: Which of the following is NOT an ore of manganese?
x: Ilmenite is a titanium ore; pyrolusite, manganite and hausmannite are manganese ores.

s: Cinnabar (HgS) is an ore of which metal?
x: Cinnabar is mercury sulphide; galena is lead, chalcopyrite copper and zinc blende zinc.

s: What is the chemical formula of iron pyrites?
x: Iron pyrites is FeS₂; magnetite is Fe₃O₄, siderite FeCO₃ and limonite FeO(OH)·nH₂O.

s: Which of the following ore–formula pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cassiterite is SnO₂. Zinc blende is ZnS, cinnabar is HgS and argentite is Ag₂S.

s: Na₃AlF₆ is the chemical formula of which mineral?
x: Cryolite is Na₃AlF₆. Ilmenite is FeTiO₃, corundum is anhydrous Al₂O₃ and bauxite is Al₂O₃·xH₂O.

s: Which of the following is a sulphide mineral?
x: Galena (PbS) is a sulphide; smithsonite and calcite are carbonates and cassiterite an oxide.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Haematite is the magnetic oxide of iron.
x: Option B is incorrect: magnetite (Fe₃O₄) is the magnetic oxide of iron, while haematite is Fe₂O₃. The bauxite, galena and cryolite descriptions are right.

s: Which of the following metal–ore pairs is correctly matched?
x: Lead is obtained from galena. Mercury comes from cinnabar, silver from argentite and tin from cassiterite.

s:
Assertion (A): Talc is the softest mineral.
Reason (R): Talc is a mineral of magnesium and is a magnesium silicate.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: being a magnesium silicate does not by itself make talc soft; its weakly bonded layers do.

s: What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
x: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; limestone and calcite are CaCO₃ and fluorspar CaF₂.

s: Malachite is an ore of which metal?
x: Malachite, Cu₂(CO₃)(OH)₂, is a copper ore; zinc is from zinc blende, mercury from cinnabar, manganese from pyrolusite.

s: Cassiterite (SnO₂) is an ore of which metal?
x: Cassiterite is the ore of tin; tungsten is from wolframite, titanium from ilmenite and rutile, thorium from monazite.

s: Haematite and magnetite are ores of which metal?
x: Iron comes from haematite and magnetite; aluminium from bauxite, copper from chalcopyrite and zinc from zinc blende.

s: Which alloy contains about 60% copper, 20% nickel and 20% zinc?
x: German silver is copper 60, nickel 20 and zinc 20; it contains no silver.

s: Which of the following fossil sites is wrongly matched with its State?
x: The Siwalik Fossil Park at Saketi is in Sirmur, Himachal Pradesh, not Uttarakhand.

s: Where is the Marine Gondwana Fossil Park, a National Geological Monument, located?
x: The Marine Gondwana Fossil Park, with Lower Permian marine fossils, is at Manendragarh, Chhattisgarh.

s: What type of lake is Lonar Lake?
x: Lonar Lake is a meteorite crater lake.

s: In which State is the Siwalik Fossil Park, Saketi, located?
x: The Siwalik Fossil Park at Saketi is in Sirmur district, Himachal Pradesh.

s: Which group of Indian rocks contains abundant marine fossils?
x: Dravidian (Palaeozoic) rocks have abundant marine fossils, while Archaean rocks formed before life and are generally fossil-free.

s: Archaean rocks are fossil-free mainly because they:
o: Are the youngest rocks of India
x: Archaean rocks formed before life existed, so they contain no fossils.

s: Who coined the term 'Archaean', and when?
o: The Geological Survey of India in 1851
x: J.D. Dana coined the term ‘Archaean’ in 1872.

s: In which year was the Geological Survey of India, under the Ministry of Mines, set up?
x: The GSI was set up in 1851 under the Ministry of Mines.

s: Who grouped Indian rocks and prepared the Indian geological time scale?
x: Sir T.H. Holland of the GSI grouped Indian rocks; Dana coined 'Archaean' but did not prepare the Indian scale.

s: Approximately what proportion of India’s coal is held by the Gondwana rocks?
x: Gondwana rocks hold nearly 98 percent of India’s coal.

s: How does Gondwana coal compare with Carboniferous coal?
x: Gondwana coal is younger and has lower carbon content than Carboniferous coal, and is not confined to the Himalayas.

s: The Dharwar system is regarded as economically the most important mainly because it contains significant deposits of:
o: Coal, chalk and coral limestone only
Petroleum, natural gas and gypsum only
Iron ore, manganese, copper, lead and gold
x: The Dharwar system contains high-grade iron ore, manganese, copper, lead and gold and is economically the most important system.

s: Which set contains only important coal-bearing valleys associated with the Gondwana system?
x: Important Gondwana coal deposits occur in the Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys.

s: The Deccan Trap is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: End-Cretaceous basalt from fissure eruptions and black cotton soil
Upper Carboniferous limestone and marine fossils
x: The Deccan Trap formed from basaltic fissure eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous and is associated with black cotton or regur soil.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tertiary rock system of India?
o: It spans roughly the Eocene to Pliocene
The Neyveli lignite belongs to the Gondwana system
The Himalayas were born during the Tertiary period
The petroleum of Assam and Gujarat is associated with it
x: Neyveli lignite is Tertiary, not Gondwana; the other statements about the Tertiary system are correct.

s: Which of the following Indian rock systems is the youngest?
x: The broad order from older to younger is Archaean, Dharwar, Cuddapah, Gondwana, Deccan Trap and Tertiary.

s: To which group do the Cuddapah and Vindhyan systems belong?
x: Cuddapah and Vindhyan are Purana (Proterozoic) systems with a broadly similar age span; Cuddapah is not Archaean.

s: The Cuddapah system of rocks is mainly composed of which one of the following?
x: The Cuddapah system (Purana, ~1,400-600 million years) is sedimentary - shale, slate, quartzite and limestone; shales and slates are clay rocks, so the key was 'clay'. Basalt is the Deccan Trap rock, granite is typical of the Archaean, and coal belongs to the Gondwana system.

s: Which is the uppermost series of the Vindhyan system?
x: From lower to upper the Vindhyan series are Semri, Kaimur, Rewa and Bhander, so Bhander is the uppermost.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Cuddapah system?
o: It belongs to the Purana group
It is mainly made of clay rocks such as shale and slate
It is a major source of coal
x: The Cuddapah system has no coal; nearly 98% of India's coal is in the Gondwana system.

s: The Neyveli lignite belongs to which rock system?
x: Neyveli lignite is Tertiary, not Gondwana; Tertiary rocks also hold the petroleum of Assam and Gujarat.

s: Which is the oldest rock system of India?
x: The Archaean system, older than 2,500 million years, is the oldest; the Tertiary is the youngest.

s: Which rock system of India is known for the Panna diamonds?
x: The Vindhyan (Purana) system of sandstone and limestone holds the Panna diamonds of Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which State has the largest area of black cotton (regur) soil formed from Deccan Trap basalt?
x: Regur soil forms from the weathering of Deccan Trap basalt, which covers most of the Maharashtra plateau.

s: Gondwana rocks are the main source of which mineral in India?
x: Gondwana rocks hold coal; Dharwar rocks copper, Tertiary rocks petroleum and gas, and metamorphic rocks garnet.

s: Which rock basin of Andhra Pradesh is associated with barytes, asbestos, diamond and uranium?
x: The Cuddapah basin has barytes, asbestos, copper, iron, lead, diamond and uranium.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt – Bauxite, manganese and graphite
Cuddapah basin – Gold and iron ore
x: The Cuddapah basin is associated with barytes and asbestos; gold and iron ore are linked with the Dharwar system.

s: Which rock system forms India's oldest metamorphic schist belts, rich in iron ore and gold?
x: The Dharwar system forms the oldest schist belts; Gondwana rocks lie in the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari basins.

s: With which minerals is the Dharwar system of Andhra Pradesh mainly associated?
x: The Dharwar system (over 2,500 million years old) holds iron ore and gold; barytes and asbestos belong to the Cuddapah basin.

s: Which series forms the Lower Vindhyan system?
x: Semri is the Lower Vindhyan; Kaimur, Rewa and Bhander make up the Upper Vindhyan.

s: For what are the Archaean and Dharwar rocks of India chiefly known?
x: Archaean and Dharwar rocks hold metallic minerals. Gondwana rocks hold coal, Tertiary rocks petroleum and Cuddapah rocks barytes and asbestos.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Central belt — Bailadila iron ore and Balaghat manganese
Southern belt — Iron ore, gold, manganese and chromite
North-Eastern belt — Gold and lignite as its principal minerals
Chota Nagpur — Coal, iron ore and mica
x: The North-Eastern belt is associated with Assam crude oil and Meghalaya coal and limestone. Gold and lignite are characteristic of the Southern belt in the listed classification.

s: In which minerals is the North-Eastern Plateau mineral belt of India rich?
o: Coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper
x: The North-Eastern Plateau belt is rich in coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper.

s: Which States does the Central mineral belt of India, with iron ore, manganese, coal and limestone, mainly cover?
x: The Central belt covers Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, with iron ore (Bailadila), manganese (Balaghat), coal and limestone.

s: Neyveli in the Southern mineral belt is a major area of which mineral?
x: Neyveli is a major lignite area of the Southern belt, which also has iron ore, gold, manganese and chromite.

s: With which of the following is Digboi in Assam associated?
x: Digboi is an oilfield; Zawar has zinc and Tummalapalle in AP has uranium.

s: In the South-Western Plateau mineral belt, for which mineral is Kerala noted?
x: The belt spans Karnataka, Goa, the TN uplands and Kerala; Kerala is noted for monazite.

s: For which minerals is the North-Western (Aravalli) mineral belt mainly known?
o: Non-ferrous minerals such as copper and lead-zinc
x: The North-Western belt is known for non-ferrous minerals, plus gypsum, salt, limestone and Gujarat's petroleum.

s: India's chromite is mined in the Sukinda Valley of which State?
x: Chromite comes from the Sukinda Valley, Odisha.

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Mineral — Principal deposit area
x: Keonjhar and Bonai in Odisha are iron-ore areas. Sundargarh and Kendujhar are manganese areas (not copper), Balaghat and Chhindwara are MP manganese areas (not chromite), and Zawar near Udaipur is lead-zinc (not manganese).

s: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant obtains its iron ore mainly from which area?
x: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant gets its iron ore mainly from Bailadila in Chhattisgarh.

s: In which State is the Noamundi iron-ore area located?
x: Noamundi and Singhbhum are in Jharkhand; Badampahar is in Odisha, Bailadila in Chhattisgarh and Kudremukh in Karnataka.

s: Balaghat and Chhindwara in Madhya Pradesh are important areas of which mineral?
x: Balaghat and Chhindwara are manganese-bearing areas of Madhya Pradesh, as Sundargarh and Kendujhar are in Odisha.

s: For which mineral is Sukinda in Odisha famous?
x: Sukinda in Odisha is India's noted chromite area.

s: The Kudremukh iron-ore deposits of Karnataka are in which district?
x: Kudremukh is in Chikkamagaluru district.

s: Bhandara is a manganese-producing district of which State?
x: Bhandara is the manganese area of Maharashtra.

s: Krivoy Rog in Ukraine is famous for which mineral?
x: Krivoy Rog in Ukraine is a major iron-ore region.

s: To which country was iron ore from the Bailadila mines mainly exported?
x: High-grade haematite from Bailadila feeds Vizag Steel and was exported to Japan.

s: With which country's collaboration was the Rourkela Steel Plant set up?
x: Rourkela Steel Plant was built with the German firms Krupps and Demag and began production in 1959.

s: What is India's position with respect to iron ore?
o: Dependent on imports for almost all its needs
x: India is self-sufficient in iron ore and a net exporter (about 46 million tonnes exported in 2023–24).

s: Which State has the largest reserves of manganese ore in India?
x: Odisha has the largest manganese reserves; MP, Maharashtra and Karnataka are other leading States.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Karnataka is first in India in iron-ore reserves.
2. Odisha is the top producer of iron ore in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Karnataka leads iron-ore reserves while Odisha leads iron-ore production.

s: Which State holds the largest share (about 39%) of India's haematite iron-ore reserves?
x: Odisha holds about 39% of haematite reserves, then Jharkhand (19.58%) and Chhattisgarh (19.09%).

s: Didwana in Rajasthan is known for which mineral?
x: Didwana in Rajasthan is a salt source.

s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Mineral — Use
o: Dolomite — Flux in steel and refractories
x: Dolomite is used as a flux in steel production and in refractories. Kyanite and sillimanite are mainly used in refractories, while barytes is used in oil-well drilling mud.

s: Which one of the following non-metallic minerals is chiefly used in the manufacture of cement and as a flux?
x: Limestone is used in cement manufacture and as a flux. It is associated with Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

s: Sona Pahar in Meghalaya is an important source of which mineral?
x: Sona Pahar is associated with sillimanite; Lapsa Buru with kyanite and the Cuddapah basin with asbestos.

s: Mangampet in Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh is internationally notable for deposits of which mineral?
x: Mangampet in Kadapa is among the world's largest deposits of barytes. Barytes is used in oil-well drilling mud.

s: Why is mica used in the electrical and electronic industries?
x: Mica is valued as an insulator, not a conductor; it occurs in pegmatite veins in granite, gneiss and schist.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is one of India's major mica belts?
x: The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.

s: Lapsa Buru in Jharkhand is known for which refractory mineral?
x: Kyanite occurs at Lapsa Buru; sillimanite at Sona Pahar (Meghalaya).

s: For which of the following is Makrana in Rajasthan famous?
x: Makrana marble was used in the Taj Mahal and Victoria Memorial; salt comes from Didwana.

s: Which State is the chief source of gypsum, used in cement, fertiliser and plaster?
x: Rajasthan is the main gypsum area.

s: For what is barytes mainly used?
x: Barytes is used in oil-well drilling mud; asbestos for fire-proofing, kyanite for refractories, dolomite as steel flux.

s: For which mineral is Koderma in Jharkhand known?
x: Koderma lies in the Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh–Munger mica belt.

s: In which rocks does mica mainly occur in India?
o: Pegmatite veins of granite, gneiss and schist
x: Mica occurs in pegmatite veins in granite, gneiss and schist.

s: Which belt is known as the 'Capital of Mica', famous for ruby mica?
x: The Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh-Munger belt is called the Capital of Mica and is known for ruby mica.

s: Which region of India is poor in minerals because it is made of recent alluvium?
x: The Gangetic plains are recent alluvium and poor in minerals, while the peninsular plateau is mineral-rich.

s: India is described as being near self-sufficient in which one of the following minerals?
x: India is near self-sufficient in bauxite. About 75 per cent of India's lead requirements are imported.

s: In 2024-25, which State ranked second after Odisha in the value of mineral production?
x: The 2024-25 order was Odisha > Rajasthan > Chhattisgarh > Karnataka > Maharashtra.

s: India produces how many minerals?
x: India produces 95 minerals: 4 fuel, 10 metallic, 23 non-metallic, 3 atomic and 55 minor.

s: About what share of India's lead requirement is met by imports?
x: About 75% of India's lead is imported.

s: The royalty formula upheld by the Supreme Court in July 2026 uses an Average Sale Price that includes which of the following?
x: The upheld formula's Average Sale Price includes royalty, DMF and NMET; royalty itself is not a tax (MADA v. SAIL, 2024).

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India (2024)?
o: Royalty is a tax, so States cannot tax mineral-bearing land
Royalty is not a tax, and States may tax mineral-bearing land
Only Parliament may levy any tax on minerals
Offshore minerals vest in the States
x: MADA v. SAIL (2024) held that royalty is not a tax and that States may tax mineral-bearing land. Option A states the reverse, option C denies the States' power, and offshore minerals vest in the Union under Art. 297.

s: Under the recent MMDR amendment, within how many days must States approve adding a critical mineral to a lease?
x: States must approve within 30 days; the amendment also removed captive-sale limits.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the MMDR Act, 1957?
o: It is administered by the Ministry of Mines
It excludes petroleum, natural gas and atomic minerals
Major minerals in the First Schedule are regulated by the Centre
Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the Centre
x: Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the States.

s: Which of the following was a key feature of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015?
o: Replacement of the MMDR Act by the National Mineral Policy, 2019
Removal of all State powers over minor minerals
Auction-only allotment of mineral concessions and creation of DMF and NMET
Prohibition of captive mining in every circumstance
x: The 2015 amendment introduced auction-only allotment and created the District Mineral Foundation and the National Mineral Exploration Trust.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a stated feature of the 2025 amendment to the MMDR Act?
o: New minerals may be added to an existing lease.
All minor minerals were placed under exclusive Central regulation.
The limit on sale of captive-mined output was removed.
Prior central approval was removed for composite-licence auctions of specified minerals.
x: The 2025 amendment did not place all minor minerals under exclusive Central regulation. It allowed addition of new minerals to leases, removed the captive-sale limit and changed prior-approval requirements for specified composite-licence auctions.

s: What did the 2026 Bill on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land mainly seek to do?
o: Prohibit royalty collection by the Union Government
Transfer all offshore minerals to private ownership without auction
Restrict States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land through uniform rates
x: The 2026 Bill (August) sought to limit States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. This raised a fiscal federalism debate.

s: With which of the following is the Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana associated?
o: Using DMF funds for mining-affected people and areas, with yearly audit
Financing only offshore mineral exploration by private companies
Providing export subsidies for iron ore
Regulating petroleum and natural gas production
x: PMKKKY uses District Mineral Foundation funds for the welfare of mining-affected people and areas and provides for a yearly audit.

s: The National Mineral Policy, 2019 replaced which earlier policy?
x: The National Mineral Policy, 2019 replaced the National Mineral Policy, 2008.

s: Which Article of the Constitution vests offshore minerals in the Union?
x: Article 297 vests offshore minerals in the Union; the 2023 amendment allows production leases only through auction.

s: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, who regulates minor minerals?
x: Minor minerals are with the States (Section 15); major minerals are with the Centre.

s: What did the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023 introduce?
o: Grant of offshore mineral leases only by auction
Transfer of offshore minerals to the States
x: The OAMDR Amendment 2023 made offshore mineral leases auction-only.

s: India’s partnership with Australia announced in 2022 concerning critical minerals primarily relates to which minerals?
x: India’s 2022 partnership with Australia concerns lithium and cobalt.

s: Where are over 90% of India's coking-coal reserves found?
x: Over 90% of coking-coal reserves are in Jharia; it is a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957.

s: The rare-earth corridors proposed in the Union Budget 2026-27 cover Odisha, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and which other State?
x: The proposed rare-earth corridors cover Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

s: What type of scheme is the Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme, covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap?
x: It is a Central Sector scheme covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Critical Mineral Mission?
o: It targets 1,200 domestic exploration projects by 2030-31
It bars PSUs and private firms from acquiring mineral assets abroad
It aims to acquire 50 overseas mineral assets
A national stockpile is one of its tools
x: The mission supports PSU and private acquisition of mineral assets abroad.

s: KABIL, the company associated with overseas acquisition of critical mineral assets, is a joint venture of which organisations?
x: KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Limited, Hindustan Copper Limited and Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.

s: India's first list of critical minerals, released by the Ministry of Mines in June 2023, contained how many minerals?
x: The June 2023 list named 30 critical minerals; 50 is the overseas-asset target of the Critical Mineral Mission.

s: In February 2025, India signed a mineral-exploration agreement with which country, where KABIL holds lithium blocks in Catamarca province?
x: The Feb 2025 agreement was with Argentina, where KABIL holds 15,703 ha in Catamarca for lithium. Chile is India's largest supplier (mainly copper), Australia was the 2022 lithium-cobalt partner, and Bolivia is not mentioned.

s: The ‘Uncover India’ project is being undertaken by GSI in collaboration with which organisation to probe deep-seated deposits?
x: GSI’s ‘Uncover India’ project is being carried out with Geoscience Australia to probe deep-seated deposits.

s: China, the top producer of rare earth elements, accounts for about what share of rare-earth mining?
x: China is the top rare-earth producer with about 70% of mining.

s: In February 2023, GSI reported 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium at Salal-Haimana in which district?
x: The lithium find was at Salal-Haimana, Reasi (J&K); its auction was annulled for want of bids.

s: The National Critical Mineral Mission aims to acquire how many overseas mineral assets?
x: NCMM targets 50 overseas assets, 1,200 exploration projects by 2030-31 and 15+ critical minerals.

s: Rare earths comprise how many elements?
x: Rare earths are 17 elements; China accounts for about 70% of their mining.

s: Which country is India's largest supplier of copper?
x: Chile is India's largest copper supplier among its mineral partners.

s: In which district of Karnataka did the Atomic Minerals Directorate report about 1,600 tonnes of lithium resources at Marlagalla?
x: AMD (Department of Atomic Energy) reported 1,600 tonnes of lithium resources in the Marlagalla area of Mandya district.

s: Which organisation reported about 1,600 tonnes of lithium resources in the Marlagalla area of Mandya, Karnataka?
o: Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research
x: The Atomic Minerals Directorate (AMD), a unit of the Department of Atomic Energy, reported the Mandya lithium.

s: Which of the following disaster – year pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Indian Ocean Tsunami struck in 2004; Koyna was 1967, Killari 1993 and Bhuj 2001.

s: After the Indian Ocean tsunami of which year was the IOC-coordinated Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System set up?
x: The system was set up after the 2004 tsunami, with regional centres in India, Indonesia, Australia and others.

s: Which parts of India are described as the most exposed to tsunami risk?
o: The Himalayan foothills and the Rann of Kutch
The east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
The western coast and Lakshadweep Islands
The Indo-Gangetic Plain and the Western Ghats
x: India’s east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the most exposed areas to tsunami risk.

s: INCOIS, which houses the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, works under which ministry?
x: INCOIS has been an autonomous body under the Ministry of Earth Sciences since 1999.

s: Since which year has the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre at INCOIS been working?
x: ITEWC at INCOIS, Hyderabad, was set up after the 2004 tsunami and has worked since 2007.

s: Since which year has INCOIS been an autonomous body under the Ministry of Earth Sciences?
x: INCOIS has been autonomous since 1999; ITEWC within it works since 2007.

s: Which body is the focal point for the Sendai Framework and global disaster risk reduction?
x: The UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the focal point for Sendai and global DRR.

s: Where is the Asian Disaster Reduction Center (ADRC), which shares information and research on disasters, located?
x: ADRC is at Kobe, Japan; ADPC, which builds capacity, is in Bangkok.

s: Where is the Asian Disaster Preparedness Centre (ADPC) located?
x: ADPC is in Bangkok; ADRC is in Kobe, UNESCO-IOC in Paris and ITIC in Honolulu.

s:
Consider the following statements about disaster centres:
1. UNESCO-IOC is headquartered at Paris.
2. ITIC is located at Hyderabad.
3. UNDRR is located at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; ITIC is at Honolulu, not Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Tsunami Warning Centre in India is located in Hyderabad.
INCOIS stands for Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services.
The International Tsunami Information Centre is located in Hyderabad.
The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre is established in INCOIS.
x: Option C is incorrect: the International Tsunami Information Centre is in Honolulu. Hyderabad hosts INCOIS and India's tsunami warning centre.

s: In high-seismicity Himalayan zones, the collapse of hanging glaciers can trigger landslide-lake outburst floods and which other hazard?
x: Collapsing hanging glaciers in high-seismicity Himalayan zones can trigger GLOFs and landslide-lake outburst floods; coastal storm surges are not a consequence here.

s: According to the Geological Survey of India, approximately what share of India’s area is landslide-prone?
x: The GSI estimates that approximately 12.6–15 per cent of India’s area, or about 0.42 million square kilometres, is landslide-prone.

s: Why are the Western Ghats and Nilgiris prone to landslides?
x: Steep escarpments and orographic rain make the Western Ghats and Nilgiris landslide-prone, not permafrost.

s: Landslide Hazard Zonation mapping is classed as which type of mitigation measure?
x: Hazard zonation mapping is non-structural; retaining walls are structural and hill building codes regulatory.

s: Rock bolting, wire mesh, drainage improvement and slope grading are which type of landslide-mitigation measure?
x: All four are structural landslide-mitigation measures.

s: Which of the following is the appropriate regulatory measure for high-risk landslide zones?
o: Construction should be shifted to riverbanks
Construction should be permitted without regulation
x: In high-risk landslide zones, building should be restricted. The other options would increase exposure.

s: What do Landslide Hazard Zonation maps show?
o: Exact forecasts of the time of landslides
Exact forecasts of the place of landslides
Probabilistic maps showing likelihood of landslides
x: Zonation maps are probabilistic: they show likelihood, not the exact time or place of a landslide.

s: What does Landslide Hazard Zonation mean?
o: Dividing hilly areas into homogeneous units by actual or potential landslide susceptibility, hazard or risk
Deterministic prediction of the exact date of each landslide
Mapping of coastal areas exposed to tsunami
Classifying plains by their flood frequency
x: Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous units by susceptibility, hazard or risk; such maps are probabilistic, not exact forecasts. Tsunami and flood mapping are different exercises, and landslide zonation is done mostly for hilly areas.

s: Which organisation is developing a regional Landslide Early Warning System under the LANDSLIP project?
x: The Geological Survey of India is developing a regional Landslide Early Warning System under the LANDSLIP project.

s: The snow avalanche at Badrinath (Mana) in February 2025 killed workers of which organisation?
x: The Badrinath-Mana avalanche resulted in the death of Border Roads Organisation workers.

s: What type of disaster struck Kedarnath in Uttarakhand in June 2013?
x: Kedarnath (June 2013) was a cloudburst and flash flood.

s: Which of the following disaster – type pairs is correctly matched?
x: Chamoli (2021) was a rock-ice flood; Kedarnath was a cloudburst, Badrinath an avalanche and Koyna reservoir-induced.

s: How many seismic zones does India's official IS 1893 (BIS) zoning map presently have?
x: The official map has four zones: II, III, IV and V.

s: What happened to the proposed revision of India's seismic zoning map in March 2026?
o: It was extended to the islands
It was rolled back by the Centre
It was made binding on new dams only
x: The Centre rolled the revision back in March 2026 after criticism of its methodology and cost, so the four-zone map still applies.

s: Which of the following hazard – region pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Kutch is among the Zone V (highest) earthquake-prone regions, not Zone II.

s: With reference to seismic zoning in Andhra Pradesh, which statement is correct?
o: The entire State lies in Zone V.
Andhra Pradesh has no area in Zone V.
Only Visakhapatnam lies in Zone V.
All coastal districts lie in Zone V.
x: Andhra Pradesh has no area falling in Seismic Zone V.

s: The Amaravati core capital region of Andhra Pradesh falls in which seismic zone?
x: Amaravati, with Vijayawada and Guntur, is in Zone III; AP has no Zone V area.

s: Which of the following is NOT in Seismic Zone V?
x: Delhi is in Zone IV; Kutch, the North-East and Andaman and Nicobar are in Zone V.

s: The proposed, later withdrawn, revision of India's seismic zoning map added which new zone?
x: The PSHA-based revision added a Zone VI, but it was withdrawn in March 2026.

s: Which earthquake led to the 2002 revision of India's seismic zoning map?
x: The 1993 Killari quake hit a low-risk area, so in 2002 old Zone I was merged into Zone II.

s: In which year was Seismic Zone I merged into Zone II in India's seismic zoning map?
x: The 2002 revision merged Zone I into Zone II, leaving four zones (II to V).

s: Which method did the withdrawn BIS revision of the seismic zoning map use?
x: The revised map used probabilistic seismic hazard assessment and added a Zone VI before it was withdrawn in March 2026.

s: Through how many GNSS stations does the GSI monitor crustal strain in India?
x: GSI monitors crustal strain through 34 GNSS stations.
